lesson.title: Predict the Point: Break Point on a Second Serve
lesson.hook: 15-40. Their second serve is slow and sits up on your forehand. Read the point one ball at a time.
lesson.memHTML: Find the corner, then keep going back to it.
lesson.tomorrow: On a soft second serve, step in and go deep to one corner. When they scramble back, send the next ball to the corner they just left.

predict.watch: Now watch the point you pictured, played the best way.
says: Deep to their backhand. They stretch for it and can only slice it short.
Back to the corner they just left. They sprint for it and can only float a pass.
Back to the same corner. They're still running the other way. Winner.

steps.name: Their second serve
steps.sit: 15-40. A slow second serve sits up on your forehand. The server stays back.
opts: High and safe through the middle
steps.payoff: Deep to the corner makes them stretch, and all they have is a short slice.
steps.principle: A soft second serve is a chance to make them run, not to hit a winner.
steps.why: Stepping in gives you time. Deep into a corner costs them a stretch; a safe ball through the middle or a short chip hands the server a free forehand.
steps.take: Soft second serve? Step in and go deep to a corner.

lines.A: Safe and central — they step in; you're only just in time.
lines.B: Deep to the corner — they stretch and can only slice it short.
lines.C: Short — they step in and you're stretched for their reply.
lines.D: Deep, but they reach it and play the rally — you're in time.

steps.name: Their short slice
steps.sit: Their stretched slice lands short. They're racing back toward the middle.
steps.q: Where do you go with this ball?
opts: Through the middle, and follow it in
Into the open corner, and stay back
Deep to the corner they left, and follow it in
steps.payoff: Back where they came from, they sprint again and can only float a pass. You're at the net.
steps.principle: A short ball is an approach: send it where they're not heading, then come in.
steps.why: They're running to the middle. The corner they left makes them stop and turn back. Staying back gives them time to recover; the middle feeds them a pass.
steps.take: Short ball while they recover? Approach to the corner they left.

lines.A: Straight to them — they pass you.
lines.B: They reach it and the rally goes on — the chance is gone.
lines.C: They're coming forward anyway — they get it and pass you.
lines.D: They turn back, reach it and float a pass — you're set at the net.

steps.name: Their pass
steps.sit: You're at the net. Their pass floats crosscourt. They're already heading back to the middle.
opts: Back to the corner they hit from
steps.payoff: They're running the other way and can't turn in time. Winner.
steps.principle: The open court is where a recovering player is running. Volley behind them.
steps.why: By the time you volley, they've started back to the middle, so the open court is on their way. The corner they left, or a drop volley short, is out of reach.
steps.take: At the net, volley to where they're coming from, not the open court.

lines.A: They're running that way — they get it and pass you.
lines.B: Right to them — they pass you.
lines.C: Behind them — they can't turn back in time. Winner.
lines.D: Short and soft — they're too deep to reach it. Winner too.
